findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match the only defined method signature
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments: `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) {`. However, the only method with that name introduced in this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` defined in the parent class `UsernamePasswordForm` (which `UsernameForm` extends). There is no zero-argument overload anywhere in the shown diff. This will fail to compile (method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is undefined for the given arguments), breaking the build of the entire services module and blocking any test from running. The call should likely be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requiring user != null breaks anonymous/discoverable-key passkey login
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This method now gates the calls to `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in both `authenticate()` (lines 115-117) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (lines 137-140), which are invoked with `context.getUser()` as the argument. Previously, `fillContextForm` was called precisely when `context.getUser() == null` (the normal, anonymous/first-time login case that enables the discoverable-key / conditional UI passkeys flow, e.g. navigator.credentials.get with conditional mediation). With the new `user != null` requirement, `fillContextForm` is now only invoked when a user is already present in the context (the re-authentication case this PR intends to fix), and is skipped entirely for a fresh/anonymous login attempt. This removes the webauthn challenge/rpId/attribute setup needed for the base passkeys login flow, which is exercised by pre-existing tests such as `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey()` and `passwordLoginWithExternalKey()` in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest/PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, that rely on the webauthn form/attributes being present on the very first page load with no pre-selected user. The fix for re-authentication should not have been conditioned on `user != null`; the flag should simply reflect whether passkeys/webauthn is enabled, independent of whether a user has already been resolved.

findings.title: Unused import added
findings.body: The import `org.keycloak.models.credential.PasswordCredentialModel` was added by this PR but is never referenced anywhere in the file's body. This is dead code left over from the change and should be removed.
